historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (15.6% 3yr, 3.2% 5yr) diverges >30% from revenue and EPS CAGRs and is not usable: book equity is driven by ~$10.5B of cumulative buybacks and currency translation, not by retained earnings. Revenue 3yr CAGR selected instead; it includes acquisitions, and reported organic growth has run 8-11% (FY2023 10%, FY2024 8%, FY2025 10%, 9M-2026 10-11%).
historical_growth.notes: FY2025 vs FY2022 and FY2020, annual rows of the Metrics CSV. FCF CAGRs are on reported FCF less the SBC add-back (FY2025 1,196.5; FY2022 482.0; FY2020 1,350.8) and are NOT meaningful: reported operating cash flow includes customer-deposit and settlement swings (FY2023 OCF 2,101 vs FY2022 755 on near-identical earnings). Equity-award withholding is only available from 2024 so it is not in the historical series. SBC has grown slower than revenue (FY2022 121.4 -> TTM 120.7), so SBC-adjusted and reported FCF growth do not diverge.

scenario_narratives.base: Corpay delivers roughly what it has for three years: ~10% organic growth in FY2027 inside management's 9-11% framework, fading as the business matures. Corporate Payments (AP automation, cross-border FX -- now including Alpha) keeps compounding in the mid-to-high teens and becomes the largest segment; Vehicle Payments grows mid-single-digit on Brazil tolling and international fuel cards while US fuel-card volumes stay flat; Lodging stabilises. Margins hold in the mid-50s once recurring integration costs are counted. Receivables grow with volume and consume about a quarter of each incremental revenue dollar. No credit is taken for future acquisitions, and none of the cost is charged.
scenario_narratives.bull: The mix shift re-rates the business. Cross-border FX and payables sustain ~20% organic growth as Alpha is rolled into the US and Asia and the Mastercard distribution deal broadens reach; the AvidXchange call option turns out to be in the money; spend-management cross-sell lifts revenue per client. Scale on a largely fixed processing base takes EBITDA margin from 56% to 59%. EV adoption is slow enough, and mixed-fleet/EV-charging economics good enough, that Vehicle Payments keeps growing. Float income on ~$8B of customer balances holds up because rates stay higher for longer.
scenario_narratives.bear: Three company-specific things go wrong, not all at once but cumulatively. (1) Vehicle Payments, still ~43% of revenue, shrinks in real terms: lower fuel prices and spreads, EV substitution in the US and UK, and a final FTC order that restricts the late-fee and ancillary-fee practices behind a meaningful share of US fuel-card revenue. (2) Cross-border volumes stall on tariff and trade disruption, and falling policy rates cut float income on customer deposits -- revenue that drops through at ~100% margin. (3) Credit losses rise (the allowance is already up 25% in nine months) and integration of Alpha, GPS, Paymerang and Gringo costs more than planned, taking EBITDA margin from 55% to 51%. With $11.2B of debt and a buyback programme funded partly by borrowing, the equity is geared to all three.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Corpay is valued as an operating payments company on unlevered owner free cash flow built from components, because its reported cash flow statement is dominated by customer-money movements that are not the shareholders'. Three choices drive the result and each is conservative relative to the company's own framing: adjusted EBITDA is haircut for acquisition costs that recur every year; stock compensation is charged at expense plus an estimate of the cash spent withholding shares, with the count held flat; and receivables growth is charged as a working-capital outflow with the securitization facility counted as debt. Value is organic-only -- the acquisition engine that management calls the compounding model is given no credit and no cost.
key_risks_to_valuation: Net debt definition is worth ~$25/share either way: customer deposits ($8.1B) are netted against cash, leaving only $1.3B of shareholder cash against $11.2B of debt. If more of the unrestricted cash is free than assumed, value is higher; if the cross-border business needs more regulatory liquidity, lower.
Working-capital capture is poorly constrained by history (11% to 56% of incremental revenue depending on the window). Each 10 points is roughly 2-3% of equity value.
The equity-award withholding cost (~$75M/yr) is an estimate: the filing reports tax and exercise-price withholding as one number, and it tripled in 2026 on option exercises.
Base revenue removes an ESTIMATED $120M for divested businesses; UK Maintenance revenue and the tax on its gain are not yet disclosed.
Float income on customer balances is rate-sensitive and undisclosed in dollar terms in the material read; it drops through at very high margin.
The FTC consent order is not final; the $100M charge could change and the conduct remedies could affect US fuel-card fee revenue beyond the cash cost.
Contingent claims not in the bridge: TPG minimum-return guarantee on AvidXchange (up to 1.6x invested capital) and settlement of ~$3.8B notional cross-currency net-investment swaps at maturity.
Terminal value is capped at a multiple; with leverage of ~3x EBITDA a one-turn change in the exit multiple moves equity value disproportionately.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular-session close); 52-week range 271.22-479.53
data_sources.financials: CPAY_Quarterly_Q3-2026.txt (10-Q, 30 Sep 2026: balance sheet, cash flow, debt note, EPS note, non-GAAP reconciliations, liquidity, subsequent events); CPAY_Annual_FY2025.txt and FY2023 (10-K balance sheets for the working-capital history); CPAY_Metrics.csv / core_metrics and kpis (history, buybacks, cash taxes, EquityAwardTaxes)
data_sources.qualitative: CPAY_Analysis.json (2026-11-15): segment mix, guidance (FY2026 revenue $5.34-5.36B, adjusted EPS ~$28; preliminary FY2027 organic growth 9-11%), bull/bear points, recent developments

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E pro forma. Guidance midpoint $5,350M (Q3-2026 release, range $5.34-5.36B) less an ESTIMATED ~$120M of revenue from businesses no longer owned: PayByPhone Q1-2026 (~$22M; sold 31 Mar 2026) and the UK Maintenance business Jan-Oct 2026 (~$100M; sold 2 Nov 2026 for ~$800M). Maintenance revenue is not disclosed in the 10-Q -- the $100M is an estimate from the sale price and should be replaced when the FY2026 10-K recasts it.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 30 Sep 2026: 64.413M shares outstanding (balance sheet) + 0.793M dilutive securities (Q3-2026 EPS note, treasury-stock method). Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows. The 10-Q cover shows 63.972M outstanding at 30 Oct 2026; the ~0.44M October repurchases are NOT reflected because the cash that paid for them is not in the 30 Sep balance sheet either -- both anchors are kept at the same date.
inputs.cash_note: NOT the balance-sheet cash line. Cash and equivalents 3,073.0 + restricted cash 6,339.9 = 9,412.9, less customer deposits 8,070.4 = 1,342.5 of cash that belongs to shareholders. Management itself says the $3.1B 'unrestricted' cash includes customer deposits. Total debt 11,233.1 = Term Loan A 3,271.3 + Term Loan B 2,906.0 + revolver 2,755.0 + other 0.8 + Securitization Facility 2,300.0 (treated as debt; the receivables it funds are charged through wc_capture_pct). The core_metrics total_debt of 16,394 is an XBRL aggregate that includes non-debt liabilities and is not used.
inputs.interest_income_note: Corpay reports only 'Interest expense, net'; interest income on corporate cash is not separately disclosed. Not an issue for this build: the component route starts from EBITDA (pre-interest) and the company is in net DEBT, so there is no cash pile being counted twice. Float income on customer funds is operating revenue and stays in.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 30 Sep 2026. SBC expense 120.7 = FY2025 102.6 (10-K cash-flow add-back) - 9M-2025 74.8 + 9M-2026 92.9 (Q3-2026 10-Q). Corpay publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure. Shares withheld on vesting/exercise ran 92.2 in FY2025 and 196.9 in 9M-2026, but the 10-Q footnote says these cover 'tax withholding obligations AND exercise price', so only part is a real tax cash cost; ESTIMATED at ~$75M/yr (~1.4% of revenue). 120.7 + 75 = 195.7. The withheld-share amounts sit INSIDE the gross 'Repurchase of common stock' financing line (Q1-2025: repurchases 58.718 = withholdings 58.717), so they are charged here as compensation and removed from buyback_cash -- counted once.
inputs.buyback_note: TTM open-market repurchases: gross 'Repurchase of common stock' 2,319.3 (FY2025 782.8 - 9M-2025 282.6 + 9M-2026 1,819.1) less 197.2 of shares withheld for employee tax/exercise price that are compensation, not buybacks. Corpay is a heavy repurchaser (40.9M shares / $10.5B since 2016; $1.6B authorization remaining after the 22 Oct 2026 increase), so the flat count is funded many times over -- but largely with debt: total debt rose $1.2B in the same nine months.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP ~4.8%, beta ~1.15 (levered payments name with fuel, Brazil and credit exposure) -> cost of equity ~9.8%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.3-5.65% (Term Loan A / B-6 rates at 30 Sep 2026), ~4.0% after tax. Market-value weights ~73% equity / 27% debt -> ~8.2%, rounded UP to 8.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is carried by the scenario paths and weights, not by a per-scenario discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases are immaterial for an asset-light payments processor; lease cost stays inside EBITDA as reported and lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. One treatment, no double charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%). Minorities are deducted once, in the equity bridge: Mastercard's 2.3% cross-border stake at its redemption value (320.0, puttable 2027-28 at cost + 8% p.a.) and other NCI at book (46.7).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (dcf-methods routing table: operating company, US, B2B payments). Not a bank model -- Corpay holds $8.1B of customer deposits, but they are pass-through settlement and collateral balances matched by restricted cash, not funding for a loan book; they are netted against cash rather than treated as debt or as net cash. First valuation of this ticker (no prior DCF, no memory entry). KEY JUDGMENTS: (1) Reported FCF is NOT a usable base: operating cash flow swings by +/-$1B a quarter with customer deposits and settlement receivables (Q2-2026 OCF +1,470, Q3-2026 -697). last_fcf is recorded per the contract identity but the forward flows are built from components, not from it. (2) FY0 is FY2026E, year 1 is FY2027, because the valuation date is six weeks from year end and the 30 Sep balance sheet already reflects nine months of FY2026 cash. Q4-2026 free cash flow (~$400-450M, ~$6-7/share) is deliberately NOT added -- a small conservatism. (3) EBITDA margin starts ~1pt below management's 56.5% adjusted margin because 'other addbacks' (integration, deal, restructuring, legal: $96M in 9M-2026, 2.4% of revenue) recur every year at a serial acquirer. (4) Growth is organic only; no acquisition spend is modelled and no acquired revenue is credited. (5) Working capital is NEGATIVE: receivables (incl. securitized) less payables run ~46-53% of revenue; history gives an incremental capture anywhere from ~11% (FY22-24) to ~56% (FY22-25, inflated by Alpha), so -25% is used in base. (6) Buybacks are value-neutral here; see buyback_note. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print; the stock rose ~10% on the 5 Nov Q3 release.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 = midpoint of management's preliminary FY2027 organic framework (9-11%), applied to a base already stripped of divested revenue. Fades to 3.5% by year 10 as Corporate Payments (now ~41% of revenue, 16-20% organic) grows into the mix while Vehicle Payments (~43%) runs mid-single-digit.
base.margin_rationale: 9M-2026 adjusted EBITDA margin 56.5%, less ~1pt for recurring integration/deal/restructuring addbacks; drifts back to 56.5% on mix and scale. Q3's 57.4% included ~100bp of customer-fund monetization management said may not recur.
base.da_rationale: 9M-2026 D&A 8.8% of revenue, of which ~6% is acquired-intangible amortization that rolls off absent new deals (none are modelled); converges toward capex plus a residual. Lower D&A raises taxable EBIT, so the amortization tax shield is NOT perpetuated.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes paid ran ~26% of pre-tax-plus-interest income in FY2025 and ~30% in 9M-2026 (inflated by the PayByPhone gain); GAAP ETR 26.9% for 9M-2026. 27% flat on EBIT -- no abnormal shelter to ramp out of. Pillar Two is already in the run-rate.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved off the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 20%: leverage is high and rising ($11.2B debt, debt-funded buybacks), the FTC order is not final, and five acquisitions plus two divestitures are being integrated at once -- but there is no refinancing wall (maturities 2031-32 after the May 2026 amendment) and no solvency question, so it stops short of 25%+. Base 50%: the path is management's own organic framework, and organic growth has printed 8-11% for three years. Bull cut to 30%: it needs cross-border growth, margin expansion and a benign EV/fuel outcome to arrive together.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
